text: A particular interconnection between two logic gates in an IC chip runs one-half the distance across a 7.5-mm-wide die. The interconnection line is insulated from the substrate by silicon dioxide. If the line is 1.5 μm wide and the oxide (εox = 3.9εo and εo = 8.85 × 10^−14 F/cm) beneath the line is 1 μm thick, what is the total capacitance of this line assuming that the capacitance is three times that predicted by the parallel plate capacitance formula? Assume that the silicon beneath the oxide represents a conducting ground plane.

Calculate the values of K ^(′) n and K ′ p for NMOS and PMOS transistors with a gate oxide thickness of 10 nm and 5 nm. Assume that μn = 500 cm^2/V · s, μp = 200 cm^2/V · s, and the relative permittivity of the gate oxide is 3.9. (ε0 = 8.854 × 10^−14 F/cm).

(a) The n-well in a CMOS process covers an area of 1 cm × 0.5 cm, and the junction saturation current density is 500 pA/cm^2. What is the total leakage current of the reverse-biased well? If the chip has 20 million inverters, what is the total leakage current due to the reverse-biased junctions when vO = 2.5 V? Assume VDD = 2.5 V and VSS = 0 V. (c) When vO = 0 V?

Assume that the silicon beneath the oxide represents a conducting ground plane.
